data.long_meaning: The name Falvika is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Fal' meaning brightness or radiance. It is a beautiful and unique name for a baby girl in Hindu tradition. The name Falvika carries the meaning “Brightness, Radiance” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Falvika usually hope their child will grow to embody brightness, radiance and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Falvika was a demoness who was granted a boon by Lord Vishnu to take any form she desired. She chose to be a beautiful woman and lived in the forest with her companions. Lord Rama, while on his exile in the forest, encountered Falvika and was captivated by her beauty. Despite knowing that she was a demoness, he could not resist her charms. However, he managed to resist her advances and continued on his journey. This story is found in the Indian epic Ramayana.

Falvika is also mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata as the wife of Abhinava, a king of the Vidarbha region. She is described as a beautiful and virtuous woman who was deeply devoted to her husband and the god Vishnu. During the great battle of Kurukshetra, Abhinava was killed in the war. Falvika, filled with grief, performed severe penance and was granted the boon of immortality by Lord Vishnu. She then lived as a divine being, known as Pushkala-mata or the Mother of Puspaka Vimana, in the celestial realm of Svarga.
